claim.pdf_says: 8.9 Reserved words — page 237 column 1 begins 'OBJECT / OBJECT-COMPUTER / OBJECT-REFERENCE / OCCURS / OF / OFF / OMITTED / ...' and column 3 ends with 'SYSTEM-DEFAULT'. 'TABLE', 'TALLYING', 'TERMINATE', 'TEST', 'THAN' are printed on the following page.
claim.markdown_says: The page-237 slice starts at 'OFF' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:10469). The five words actually printed above it on page 237 are jammed onto the last line of the page-236 block: :10466 'NUMERIC-EDITED OBJECT OBJECT-COMPUTER OBJECT-REFERENCE OCCURS OF'. Symmetrically the slice ends at :10584 'SYSTEM-DEFAULT TABLE TALLYING TERMINATE TEST THAN'.
claim.why_it_matters: Same collapsed-line defect as page 235, occurring at both boundaries of this page. OBJECT, OBJECT-COMPUTER, OBJECT-REFERENCE, OCCURS, OF and TABLE, TALLYING, TERMINATE, TEST, THAN stop being individually addressable entries of the reserved-word list, and page attribution is off by one page in both directions.

verdict.reasoning: Both quotations are accurate, but the difference is pure line-break/page-boundary placement, not content. VERIFIED AGAINST THE RENDERS (300 dpi p237, 200 dpi p236 and p238): printed p236 (folio 206) column 3 genuinely ends at NUMERIC-EDITED; printed p237 (folio 207) column 1 genuinely begins OBJECT / OBJECT-COMPUTER / OBJECT-REFERENCE / OCCURS / OF / OFF ... and column 3 genuinely ends at SYSTEM-DEFAULT; printed p238 (folio 208) column 1 genuinely begins TABLE / TALLYING / TERMINATE / TEST / THAN / THEN. And the markdown lines are as quoted: :10466 'NUMERIC-EDITED OBJECT OBJECT-COMPUTER OBJECT-REFERENCE OCCURS OF' and :10584 'SYSTEM-DEFAULT TABLE TALLYING TERMINATE TEST THAN'. NOTHING IS MISSING, ADDED, MISSPELLED OR REORDERED. All eleven words the claim calls misplaced (OBJECT, OBJECT-COMPUTER, OBJECT-REFERENCE, OCCURS, OF; TABLE, TALLYING, TERMINATE, TEST, THAN; plus the boundary words NUMERIC-EDITED and SYSTEM-DEFAULT) are present in the transcription, spelled correctly, in correct alphabetical position within the single continuous A-Z reserved-word list; they are merely space-separated instead of newline-separated on the two boundary lines. I also count-matched the whole page-237 slice against the render block by block: OFF..OVERRIDE 13/13, PACKED-DECIMAL..PROTOTYPE 19/19, QUOTE/QUOTES 2/2, RAISE..RUN 36/36, SAME..SYSTEM-DEFAULT 39/39 — no word dropped or duplicated anywhere on the page. The transcription even faithfully preserves ISO's own out-of-alphabetical-order printing of SEND before SELF (md :10552-10553), which is direct evidence the slice was transcribed from this page rather than reconstructed. On the merits of the two sub-claims: (1) 'stop being individually addressable entries' is a property of a hypothetical line-oriented consumer of the markdown, not of the spec's content. Section 8.9 is a flat membership list whose only semantic payload is the SET of reserved words, and that set is unchanged; COBOL reserved words never contain an embedded space, so a whitespace run of them is unambiguously separable, and any extractor must whitespace-tokenize regardless because the source is a three-column layout where line structure carries no meaning to begin with. (2) The page-anchor attribution being off by five words in each direction is exactly the 'page-break furniture' the rejection criteria name: the markers are navigational scaffolding added by the transcription, and the boundary lands five entries late only as a direct consequence of the joined line. No sentence, rule, format diagram, general format, or normative statement is affected — there is no meaning to change in an alphabetical word list whose membership is intact. Under the stated bar (reject when the text is present though reflowed, when the difference is only page-break furniture or line wrapping, and when meaning is unchanged) this is a transcription-hygiene nit at cosmetic severity, not a structural content discrepancy. It is worth a one-line cleanup if the page slices are ever regenerated, but it is not a defect in the spec transcription's content and it cannot mislead an implementer about any COBOL semantics.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The claim's quotations of both sources are accurate and the collapsed lines do exist (md :10466 and :10584), but every affected reserved word is present, correctly spelled and correctly alphabetically ordered; only the newline-vs-space separator on the two page-boundary lines, and the consequent five-word-late placement of the page-237 anchor, differ. Reclassify from kind=misplaced-content / severity=structural to a cosmetic line-splitting nit in the page-slicing step (fix by splitting the joined boundary lines when slices are regenerated). No reserved word, rule, or general format is altered.
